description: An exemption is a named class of reason for which an analyzer keeps a symbol the reference graph alone would report. Each class has a detection rule an analyzer computes from its language's type information and program graph, never from a text search except where a class says so; the analyzer records the class name in the symbol's `retained_by` field, lists the held-back symbols and their classes on request, and lets a maintainer disable any class by name so an exemption suspected of hiding a defect can be tested. Every recorded exemption names the source site its evidence was found at and carries one clause of detail naming the relation and the thing it relates to, `satisfies io.Writer` or `named by {{.Title}}`: a class derived from a type relation names the conversion or the consumer site, a class derived from a text match names the position of the matching text, the generated-file class names the package clause of a generated Go file and the first line of a generated TypeScript file, and the assembly and plugin class names the assembly directive, or the package clause of the file that declares the symbol where the evidence is the shape of the package. An exemption's evidence site decides which run records it: under a production sweep, which counts no reference from a test file, an exemption whose evidence site is in a test file does not hold, for every class in this file. A conversion, an encoder or template destination, a directive, a generated-file clause or a matching text in a test file retains nothing for production, exactly as a reference from a test file makes nothing live for production, and it counts as a test reference to each symbol it would retain, as a reference from a test file does: the symbol is reported under the code its production and test references select, so a symbol that production code never references and that such evidence alone retains is reported as test-only use rather than under an unused code; a run that counts test references records the exemption. The vocabulary is closed: a conformance expectation whose `retained_by` names a class absent from this file is a defect in the expectation. Fields: `languages` names the languages the class runs on (`go`, `ts`); `confidence` uses the report's reachability vocabulary, `certain` for a class derived from a type relation and `possible` for a class derived from a text match; `rule` is the detection rule stated for an implementer in any language; `mechanism` restates it in each listed language's own terms; `retains` names what the class keeps. `typescript_visibility` is present on every class that runs on TypeScript and states whether the class can retain a class member declared with the `private` modifier and whether it can retain one declared with a `#private` name; a class that retains no class member states false for both. The two differ at runtime: `private` is a compile-time constraint only, so a `private` member stays reachable by its name through a string index, a decorator, a container or a serializer, while a `#private` name cannot be named from outside its class body at all. Every class that reaches members by name therefore applies to `private` and not to `#private`, and a `#private` member with no reference in its own class body is reported whatever else the program does.

exemptions.rule: A method is retained when a value of its receiver's type reaches a position typed as an interface the method helps satisfy and the interface method it implements is called. The analyzer records every site, in the target and in each loaded consumer, where a value of type T is converted or assigned to an interface type I (an explicit conversion or a satisfaction assertion, an assignment, an argument, a return value, an element stored in an I-typed container), and every instantiation whose type argument T stands for a type parameter whose constraint is I, because the generic code calls the constraint's methods on values of T. In a Go library, a site grammar/analysis.md "Conversions an outside program writes" records at a published parameter or at a type parameter of a published declaration, converting each type an outside program can hold to the interface type or instantiating the type parameter with it, is a site of the set. In Go, a type assertion or a type switch case naming an interface J, written in the target or a loaded consumer on an operand whose type is an interface K, derives a site converting T to J for each type T that implements J and whose value reaches K: a site of the set converts T to K, or converts T to an interface I from which a chain of sites of the set leads to K, each site of the chain converting a value of the interface type the previous one converts to, the first a value of type I. One site is derived per such site or chain, held by the declaration holding the assertion and by every declaration holding a site it derives from. A value that reaches only an interface from which no chain leads to K derives nothing there, whatever else it implements. A call of `errors.As` whose second argument has type pointer to J, and a call of `errors.AsType` instantiated with J, J an interface type, is read as a type assertion of J on the call's first argument, which is an error, here and in every clause of this class that reads type assertions. The reading is an abstraction of the call, which also tests each error its first argument wraps and asks an `As` method: a wrapped error counts where a site of the set brings its type to `error` as above, and an `As` method is retained by the errors-duck-typing class. For each recorded (T, I) pair, it retains each member of T that I requires, except a method that implements a method of I the rule of DS1203 holds for and its precondition does not exempt. In Go, where I is a defined interface type declared outside the analyzed program, code outside the analysis holds the value through I and may assert another interface on it, so the pair also retains each method by which T implements an interface that the source of the package declaring I asserts, being the interface type each type assertion and each type switch case in that source names, whichever package declares it, an interface type literal included. Where the site is an argument of a call whose callee is a function or a method a package outside the analyzed program declares, the callee holds the value through its parameter and may assert another interface on it, so the pair also retains, in the same way, each method by which T implements an interface the source of the callee's package asserts. That source is read and no other: a package the callee hands the value on to is not, a modelling bound. Where a site of the set converts T to `error`, code outside the analysis may assert on that error an interface J that holds `error`'s method, so the pair also retains each method by which T implements J, J being a non-generic defined interface type that a package outside the analyzed program declares, that embeds `error` or declares its `Error() string` method and that the type the site converts implements, a value of T not counting for a method only a pointer to T has, where the source of the package declaring J asserts J itself, in a type assertion, a type switch case, or a call of `errors.As` or `errors.AsType` read as above. Only the source of a package declaring such a J is read for this, and only its assertions of J count, a modelling bound, and a generic interface is not read for this either. A site retains as a use by the declaration that holds it, so a retained method is live only while that declaration is, and it falls into that declaration's dead component with it. A site the analysis derives from other sites, an assertion's and a chain's among them, is held by every declaration that holds one of those sites. Under reference-counting it is a use by each of them. Under reachability it retains only while every one of them is live, and where one of them is dead, a member that only such sites retain falls into that declaration's dead component. A derived site one of whose sites is written in a test file is evidence in a test file. A derived site is a site of the set, so sites are derived until no further site joins. A satisfaction assertion is a root while T is built by live code, being referenced by a declaration other than a satisfaction assertion that is live without the assertion, applied until no further declaration joins, and its pair then retains as any other does. The assertion of a type only dead code builds is no root and retains nothing: it falls with T, so the type, its methods and the assertion delete together. The assertion is not a use of I beyond itself: when nothing else uses I as a type, I is still reported as an unused satisfaction assertion, each method of I is reported under DS1203, and the methods of T that implement them fall with those findings.
exemptions.retains: For each recorded (T, I) pair, the members of T that I requires, and each embedded field of T, and of the types embedded in turn, through which a member I requires is promoted to T, except a method implementing a method of I that DS1203 reports, while every declaration holding the site is live. In Go, where I is declared outside the analyzed program, the methods by which T implements an interface a type assertion or a type switch case in the source of the package declaring I names, as well, and at a site that is an argument of a call of a function or a method declared outside the analyzed program, the methods by which T implements an interface such an assertion or case in the source of the callee's package names, and at a site converting T to `error`, the methods by which T implements an interface holding `error`'s method that a package outside the analyzed program declares and its own source asserts.

mechanism.go: Build the conversion set from the type-checked program: an assertion of the form `var _ I = (*T)(nil)` or `var _ I = T{}`, a value passed to a parameter of type I, a value returned into a result of type I, a value assigned to a variable or field of type I, an element stored into an I-typed slice, map, channel or struct field, and a type argument T of an instantiation whose type parameter's constraint is I, and in a library, the site grammar/analysis.md "Conversions an outside program writes" records at each parameter of a published function whose type is an interface type I, the element type of a variadic parameter included, and at each type parameter of a published function or of an exported generic type whose constraint is an interface type I, for each non-interface type T of the target that an outside program can hold, as that section states, and that implements I under that section's two modelling bounds, held by the declaration of the parameter or the type parameter and recorded only while the published API's class is below `certain`. A type assertion `x.(J)`, a type switch case naming J, and a call `errors.As(err, &j)` whose second argument has type `*J` or `errors.AsType[J](err)`, J an interface type, written in the target or a loaded consumer, on an operand whose type is an interface K (`error` for the two calls), adds the pair (T, J) for every T, or pointer to it, that implements J as `types.Implements` decides and whose value reaches K: a site of the set converts it to K, or converts it to an interface I and a chain of sites of the set converts a value of type I to K, each site through the interface type the previous one converts to. It adds one derived site per such site or chain, held by the declaration holding the assertion together with every declaration holding a site of it, and evidence in a test file where one of them is written in one. A derived site is a site of the set, so pairs are added until no further pair joins. For each (T, I) pair, `types.Implements(T, I)` decides satisfaction, and the methods of T that I requires are retained, except a method implementing a method of I that DS1203 reports. A method promoted to T through embedded fields retains each embedded field its selection passes through as well, with the same holders, because deleting one of them removes the method from T's method set. Each is a use by the declaration that holds the site. Where I is a defined interface type of a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, retain as well every method by which T, or a pointer to it, implements an interface that package's source asserts, as `types.Implements` decides: the interface type of each type assertion `x.(J)` and of each type switch case written in that package's source, and the interface J of each call `errors.As(err, &j)` whose second argument has type `*J` and of each call `errors.AsType[J](err)` written there, whichever package declares it, an interface type literal among them. Where the site is an argument of a call, the value reaching a parameter of a function or a method that a package neither the target nor a loaded consumer declares, a call through an interface value naming the interface's method and its package, retain in the same way every method by which T, or a pointer to it, implements an interface that the callee's package's source asserts. No package the callee hands the value on to is read. Where a site of the set converts T to `error`, retain as well, for each non-generic defined interface type J that a package of the target's build that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer declares, whose method set holds `Error() string`, by embedding `error` or by declaring the method, and that the type the site converts implements as `types.Implements` decides, T for a value of T and `*T` for a pointer, every method by which that type implements J, where that package's source writes a type assertion `x.(J)`, a type switch case naming J, a call `errors.As(err, &j)` whose second argument has type `*J` or a call `errors.AsType[J](err)`. Each is a use by the declaration that holds the site converting T to `error`. For this the analysis reads the source of a package only where the package declares such a J, and reads there only the assertions of J. A type assertion or a case naming a type that is not an interface asserts nothing. The analysis reads each such package's source for its type assertions, its type switches and those two calls alone, wherever in that source they stand and whatever value they assert on. A generic interface type that is not instantiated is skipped, and so is an interface that holds a type term or embeds `comparable`. An assertion of a type that no live declaration other than an assertion references is no root, retains nothing and falls with the type. A type registered with `flag.Var`, or used as an `io.Writer`, an `http.RoundTripper` or a `sort.Interface`, is an ordinary member of the conversion set, so those methods are retained here and by no other class.
mechanism.ts: Build the same conversion set over class instance types flowing into interface-typed positions, an interface here being an interface declaration, an object type literal a type alias names, or such a literal that is a constituent of an intersection a type alias names: an `implements` clause, an assignment, an argument, a return value, an element stored in an interface-typed container, and a type argument whose type parameter's constraint is the interface. For each (class, interface) pair, the checker's assignability test decides satisfaction, and the members the interface requires are retained, except a method that implements a method of that interface DS1203 reports. Each is a use by the declaration that holds the site, the class itself for an `implements` clause.

exemptions.rule: A type whose values reach a consumer that inspects them by name at runtime has the members that consumer reads retained, on the type and on every type the consumer walks to through its fields, the types the program stores in an interface-typed field included. An encoder's argument that is a composite literal reaches the type of each value the literal writes into an interface-typed position, and an argument whose type is a defined interface type reaches every type the program converts to that interface. A conversion to any reaches no destination by itself. What is retained is per destination. A destination that reads fields retains the exported fields and the tagged fields, except a field an encoder skips because its tag gives it the key `-`, while a decoding destination fills fields through reflection, which is neither a read nor a write of this contract, and retains none of them, the `XMLName` field an XML decoder compares excepted. A function that only decodes into its argument is a decoding destination and reads no field, wherever it is declared, save a field of a pointer, interface or map type that the program writes, which the decoder reads to decode into the value the field holds. Each destination retains the methods it resolves by name and no other method, so a type only decoding destinations reach keeps the decoding methods they resolve and no other method. A consumer the analysis cannot read counts as one that reads every field and resolves by name the methods its own code can name: a value passed as an argument to a parameter typed as the empty interface of a function or method outside the analyzed program, a slice, an array or a map of such values included, has left the analysis, because that parameter keeps nothing of the value's type, while a value passed to any other interface-typed parameter is a conversion interface-satisfaction answers. So has a value returned as an interface-typed result by a method that implements a method of an exported interface declared outside the analyzed program, because outside code calls that method through the interface. Code outside the analysis may read the fields of such a value and call the methods by which it satisfies an interface the callee's package declares or writes as a literal, exported or not, or an exported interface of a package in that package's import closure or of a package outside the analyzed program that imports the callee's package. A standard container stores the value and hands it back to the program unchanged, so the code of its own package is the only outside code that reads the value: such a value keeps the methods by which it satisfies an interface that package declares or writes as a literal and no field and no other method. A type passed as a type argument, written or inferred, to a generic function, method or type declared in a package outside the analyzed program, where that package's own direct imports name a standard decoder, reaches a decoding destination of that decoder, whether or not the generic's body decodes it. A value stored in an interface-typed place, or in a place holding interface values, that is itself a composite literal, a field or a variable of a slice, array or map type whose elements are interfaces, carries every type that container holds, so the place holds what the container holds, and so on through each container stored in it. An argument of a function outside the analyzed program that names such a container carries what it holds as well. A call of a method of an interface type holds, at an interface-typed result, what each method of the program that implements that interface method returns at that result. A destination that reads fields does not read the fields of a type whose method set holds the encoding method that destination calls for its direction, and does not walk on through them: the encoder calls the method instead. A method with a pointer receiver counts only where every value of the type the walk meets is addressable. A function or method outside the analyzed program whose name says it fills the value it is given from a document fills its fields and may read them, so it retains none of them, and a finding about a field such a callee alone fills is at the reachability class possible, because whether the callee also reads the field, as a validating binder does, the analysis cannot see. So does a function or method outside the analyzed program handed a pointer to a struct value at an empty-interface parameter, which may fill it whatever its name, and a generic function outside it whose type parameter its results name and none of its parameters does, which makes the value it returns: a field nothing writes that only such a callee fills is at the reachability class possible. A callee whose own body hands the value to a destination that reads fields is a destination that reads every field. An assertion to an interface type of a struct field's value that reflection reads is a conversion of each exported field type of that struct that implements the interface, whichever field the index or the name selects, so it retains the methods by which each implements it.
exemptions.retains: The exported fields and the struct fields carrying a tag on every type that flows into a destination that reads fields and on every defined type reached from those types' fields through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, an embedded field, or an interface-typed field, element or value through the types the program stores there, and on the types an argument's own composite literals write into its interface-typed positions and, for an argument of a defined interface type, every type the program converts to that interface, except that a standard encoder does not read a field its tag gives the key `-`. An embedded struct field, exported or not, for a destination that reads fields. The encoding and decoding methods a standard encoder or decoder resolves by name, in the direction it runs, and no other method of a type only decoders reach. The `XMLName` field, for an XML decoder. A field of a pointer, interface or map type that the program writes, for a decoder. The `LogValue` method for a `log/slog` destination. The exported methods for a template engine and for a method-reaching reflection call. In Go, where every template that receives the value is one the analysis reads, a template engine reads only the fields and the methods those templates name, an embedded field, and the `String`, `Error` and `Format` methods the engine prints a value through, and it reads the same of each type a method it calls returns: the program executes the set directly from a variable that one chain of the engine's constructors, parses and lookups writes, over constant text, constant file names or patterns resolved against the target root or the calling file's directory and constant patterns of an embedded file system, and that the program reads only to execute, look up or name its templates. A library's set, an `html/template` set holding a JavaScript context, a script element or an event-handler attribute, whose engine encodes a value there whole, and a set reached through any other expression read every field. For a destination outside the analyzed program, the fields, the encoding and decoding methods of both directions, and every method by which the type satisfies an interface the callee's package declares or writes as a literal, or an exported interface that a package in its import closure or a package outside the analyzed program that imports it declares, or every exported method where the callee's package's imports reach a template engine. For a standard container, the methods by which the type satisfies an interface its own package declares or writes as a literal, and no field. For a type argument reaching an outside generic, what a decoding entry point of each standard decoder that generic's package directly imports retains.

mechanism.go: A type T flows into the class when a value of T, or a pointer to one, reaches one of the destinations below. Retain on T the members that destination retains, and retain the same members on every defined type reached from the fields of a retained type through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, or an embedded field, applied until no further type joins. A destination that reads fields reads only a field production code writes, by a composite literal, keyed or positional, an assignment, an increment or a decrement, or a conversion that produces a value of the field's struct type, or of a struct type that holds it by value, from a value of another type, the writes of test files counting too where the run counts test references, and an embedded field, which a write of a promoted field writes through, as `analysis.md` states for a member of a type the program sends: a field nothing writes is judged by its own references. A field a decoding destination of production code fills, a decoding entry point, a function that only decodes into its argument, a callee whose name says it fills its argument, a callee outside the analyzed program handed a pointer to the value at an empty-interface parameter, or a generic function outside it whose type parameter its results name and none of its parameters does, for the type argument that parameter binds, is read as a written field is, wherever the walk meets that destination, though the fill is no write of the read-and-write classification, because a value decoded and encoded again carries what the decoded document held. A field a destination would read that production code never writes, where the destination is a function or method outside the analyzed program whose name says it fills its argument, or one handed a pointer to the value, is a field that callee fills, as below. A field, an element or a map value of an interface type reaches the types of the values the program stores in it: a value converted to that interface type where it is the field's value in a composite literal, the right side of an assignment to the field, an element of a composite literal of the slice, array or map type, an argument of `append` onto it, or the right side of an assignment to an index of it. Where the stored value is an interface-typed parameter of the enclosing function, it stands for every argument a call of that function passes for that parameter, applied until no further argument joins, and a parameter no call of the program passes adds no type. The argument of a destination reaches more types of its own. Where the argument expression, read through parentheses, conversions and the address operator, is a composite literal, it reaches the type of each value the literal writes into an interface-typed position, a map key or value, a slice or array element or a struct field, keyed or positional, and so on through each composite literal it nests, whatever type the literal has. Where the argument's static type is a defined interface type, it reaches every type the program converts to that interface type, at the sites `interface-satisfaction` records. The same holds for each argument a call passes for an interface-typed parameter of a function of the program that is itself a destination. An interface-typed argument of a destination, or of an outside function's empty-interface parameter, carries each concrete type the program stores in what it names. A parameter of the enclosing function holds what every call passes for it. An interface-typed variable holds what the program assigns to it, a call's results included. A read of an interface-typed field holds what the program stores in that field. A call of a function or a method of the program holds what its return statements put at that result, a function literal's returns excepted. A call through a function value holds what every function or method of the program used as a value, a bound method value and a method expression among them, returns at that result, where its result count is the call's. Which function a function value holds is not followed, so that sentence retains more. A conversion to `any`, or to an interface type literal, adds no type to an argument. The encoding entry points, being the functions and methods of `encoding/json`, `encoding/json/v2`, `encoding/xml` and `encoding/gob` whose names start with `Marshal` or `Encode`, read fields: retain each walked type's exported fields and tagged fields, except a field whose tag for that encoder, `json` for `encoding/json` and `encoding/json/v2` and `xml` for `encoding/xml`, is exactly `-`, which the encoder skips, while a tag of `-,` names the key `-` and is read. An embedded field whose type is a struct or a pointer to one is read whether or not it is exported, because the encoder promotes the embedded struct's fields. Retain as well the methods the encoder resolves by name, being `MarshalJSON`, `MarshalJSONTo`, `MarshalText` and `AppendText` for JSON, `MarshalXML`, `MarshalXMLAttr` and `MarshalText` for XML, and `GobEncode` and `MarshalBinary` for gob. The decoding entry points, whose names start with `Unmarshal` or `Decode`, fill fields through reflection, which is neither a read nor a write of this contract, so they retain no field. They retain the methods the decoder resolves by name, being `UnmarshalJSON`, `UnmarshalJSONFrom` and `UnmarshalText` for JSON, `UnmarshalXML`, `UnmarshalXMLAttr` and `UnmarshalText` for XML, and `GobDecode` and `UnmarshalBinary` for gob. A decoding entry point of `encoding/xml` also retains a field named `XMLName` of type `xml.Name`, which the decoder compares with the element's name. A type argument is a decoding destination too. A type the program passes as a type argument, written or inferred, to a generic function, a generic method or a generic type declared in a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, where that package's own import declarations name `encoding/json`, `encoding/json/v2`, `encoding/xml` or `encoding/gob`, flows into a decoding entry point of each of those packages it names. It is recorded at the instantiation, with the detail naming the generic. The type arguments are read through every instantiation the program holds: a type parameter of a generic declaration of the program, passed on as a type argument, stands for each type argument an instantiation of that declaration the program holds gives it, applied until no further type joins. The analysis does not follow the type parameter through the generic's body, so the type reaches the destination whether or not that body decodes it. The destination retains decoding methods, the `XMLName` field and the fields of a pointer, interface or map type the program writes, and reads no other field, so a field that only such a decode fills is still reported. Only the generic's own package's direct imports count: a package it imports that in turn imports a decoder adds nothing. A generic function of a destination package, `reflect.TypeFor` among them, reaches that destination with each type argument an instantiation gives it, as a value of that type would. A value whose type is a type parameter, or is built from one, reaches a destination as a value of each type argument the program's instantiations give that parameter. Those type arguments are read through the type parameters of other generic declarations the parameter is passed on to, and through a generic method's receiver type parameters, applied until no further type joins. A decoding entry point reads a field of a pointer, interface or map type that the program writes anywhere, because the decoder decodes through the value the field holds, and that field is then no write-only field. An embedded field is a field to this rule, so a decoding entry point keeps it live only as it keeps any field, and it is otherwise live while a selector the program writes promotes one of its members. A field only a decoder fills and nothing reads is therefore reported, and a type only decoding entry points reach keeps the methods they resolve and no other method, whatever interfaces it satisfies. A function or method only decodes into one of its parameters when its body uses that parameter at least once, and only as an argument, unchanged or converted to an interface type, of a decoding entry point or of a function that only decodes into that argument, applied until no further function joins. A function with no body, or whose body never uses the parameter, does not. It is a decoding entry point for that parameter wherever it is declared. For a function outside the analyzed program, the analysis reads the body from the source the build list holds, for this rule alone. In a program that calls `(*json.Decoder).DisallowUnknownFields`, or passes the `json.RejectUnknownMembers` option, anywhere, a decoding entry point of `encoding/json` or `encoding/json/v2` retains the fields an encoding entry point retains as well, because the decoder then refuses a document that names a member the type lacks. Any other function or method of those four packages, a registration among them, retains what both directions retain. Fields alone are retained for a destination that reads fields and resolves no method by name: a `database/sql` `Scan` target, an argument of `reflect.DeepEqual`, and an argument of any function or method of `reflect` other than the method-reaching calls below. Fields and the `LogValue() slog.Value` method are retained for a `log/slog` destination: an argument of a `log/slog` logging function, of `slog.With`, of a `*slog.Logger` method, `With` among them, of `(*slog.Record).Add` or of an attribute constructor. An argument for a parameter of type `context.Context`, of any destination of this class, reaches no destination, whatever its type and whatever it holds: a handler reads a context's values by key and never walks one by reflection. A handler resolves `LogValue` by the value's own shape and not through a conversion, so no conversion exists for another class to read and this class is the only one that retains it. Fields and exported methods are retained for a destination that resolves a method by name: an argument of a function or method of `text/template` or `html/template`, and a value reaching a method-reaching `reflect` call, being `Method`, `MethodByName` or `NumMethod` on a `reflect.Value` or a `reflect.Type`, or a `reflect.Value` the program calls a method through. A call of a function of `reflect` whose result is the receiver of a chain of method calls of `reflect.Value` or `reflect.Type`, none of them `Method`, `MethodByName` or `NumMethod`, the last of which returns neither a `reflect.Value` nor a `reflect.Type`, reaches no method-reaching call, so its argument has its fields retained and no method, as in a program that names no method finder. This holds for a call in a function of the program that forwards its parameter there too. So does such a call whose result a local variable of the function takes by an assignment or a variable declaration, where every use of the variable heads such a chain or is given on to another such variable. Any other such call, its result held in any other variable, passed or returned among them, may reach one. At a call of `Execute` or `ExecuteTemplate` whose receiver is a variable written once by a chain of `New`, `Must`, `Parse`, `ParseFiles`, `ParseGlob`, `ParseFS`, `Funcs`, `Option` and `Lookup` whose every argument naming a template is one the analysis reads, read only as the receiver of `Execute`, `ExecuteTemplate`, `Lookup`, `Name`, `DefinedTemplates` or `Templates`, outside a library, parse each template the chain names, each file against the target root and then the calling file's directory and a `ParseFS` pattern against the files its file system holds. An argument naming a template is followed through the values it may hold: the writes of a variable whose address is never taken, the argument of the call being followed bound to a parameter of its callee, else the argument each call passes to a parameter of a function the program only ever calls by name, and the return statements of a function the program declares. The analysis reads it where each value is a constant. It reads the file system of `ParseFS` where each value is a package-level `embed.FS` variable, holding the files its `//go:embed` patterns embed, a call of `os.DirFS` whose directory is such a constant, read against the target root and then the calling file's directory and holding every regular file below it, or a call of `fs.Sub` of one with such a constant. It reads the text of `Parse` where each value is a constant or, through a string conversion, what `os.ReadFile` of a constant name, `fs.ReadFile` or a `ReadFile` method of such a file system, or `io.ReadAll` of a file its `Open` method returns gives, a name that is no constant naming any file the file system holds. At any other call of `Execute` or `ExecuteTemplate` of an engine outside a library, the templates are every template a parse function or method of that engine parses in the program, where the analysis reads each one's arguments so, the program calls no `AddParseTree` or `Delims` of the engine, names a parse method only to call it, writes no field of the engine's templates or of their parse trees and asserts no value to a type holding the engine's template, and no package outside the program that the program imports, directly or not, mentions the engine's template type in its exported API, through which a template the program does not parse could reach it. Where every one is found under the target root and parses, and no `html/template` one holds a `<script` element or a start tag with an attribute whose name starts with `on`, retain of the argument's fields only the embedded ones and those whose name an action of those templates names, and of its exported methods only those an action names and `String`, `Error` and `Format`, which the engine calls through `fmt` when it prints a value ([text/template](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template#hdr-Actions)). The engine evaluates a chain through a method, so the result type of each method retained so, walked as the argument is, reaches the same destination. A destination outside the analyzed program is a value of a struct type, a pointer to one, or a slice, an array or a map whose element, key or value type is one of these, passed as an argument to a parameter typed as the empty interface, or to a variadic parameter whose element type is the empty interface, of a function or method of a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer and that does not only decode into that argument, recorded at the call with the detail naming the callee. So is such a value returned as an interface-typed result by a method of the analyzed program that implements a method of an exported interface declared in a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, because code outside the analysis calls the method through that interface and receives the value. It is recorded at the return statement with the detail naming the interface method, and the interface's package is the callee's package below. The walk starts at every struct type the value holds. Save for deciding whether it only decodes into that argument, the analysis reads no syntax of that function, so it is read as reading every field the class retains and as resolving by name the methods its package can name: retain the encoding and decoding methods of both directions above, and every method by which the type, or a pointer to it, implements an interface the callee's package can assert, as `types.Implements` decides: each interface type the callee's package declares, exported or not, each interface type literal written in its source, and each exported interface type declared by a package in that package's import closure or by a package outside the analyzed program that the program's import closure holds and that imports the callee's package. An unexported interface of any other package is not counted. The analysis reads the callee's package's source for its interface type literals alone. A generic interface type that is not instantiated is skipped, because `types.Implements` decides no such interface. So is an interface that holds a type term or embeds `comparable`, which only constrains a type parameter. Where the callee's package's import closure holds `text/template` or `html/template`, retain every exported method as well. Any function of the analyzed program whose interface-typed parameter it passes to such a call, or to any other destination of this class, is itself a destination that retains what its destination retains, applied until no further function joins. A standard container reaches less: an argument of a method of `sync.Map`, of a method of `Value` of `sync/atomic`, or of `context.WithValue` is stored or compared and handed back to the program unchanged, and the container's own package is the only outside code that reads it. Such a value retains every method by which the type, or a pointer to it, implements an interface type that package declares or an interface type literal its source writes, and no field and no other method. A key, and an old value a `CompareAndSwap` or `CompareAndDelete` method compares, is compared as a map key is. A conversion to `sort.Interface` is an ordinary interface conversion rather than a destination of this class, so the methods that interface requires are retained by `interface-satisfaction`. Where the stored value of a store this class reads (a field's value in a composite literal, the right side of an assignment or a declaration, an element of a composite literal, an argument of `append`, the right side of an index assignment, a return statement's value at an interface-typed result, or an argument for an interface-typed parameter) is a composite literal of a slice, array or map type whose element is an interface, or a field or a variable of such a type, the place holds, beside the value's own type, every type the program stores in that literal, field or variable. An interface-typed argument of a function or method outside the analyzed program, and an argument naming such a literal, field or variable, carry the same. A call whose callee is a method of an interface type holds, at each interface-typed result, what the return statements of every method implementing it put at that result, the implementing methods being those of each non-generic package-level defined type of the target or a loaded consumer that is no interface, where the type or a pointer to it implements the method's interface as `types.Implements` decides. A return statement whose one operand is a call of several results puts each result of that call at the same position of the enclosing function's results: its concrete type where the call's result is no interface, and what the callee's result holds where it is one. Where every destination reading the fields of a value is an encoding entry point of `encoding/json`, `encoding/json/v2`, `encoding/xml` or `encoding/gob`, a defined type the walk meets whose method set holds, for every direction among those destinations, one of `MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)`, `MarshalJSONTo(*jsontext.Encoder) error` or `MarshalText() ([]byte, error)` for JSON, `MarshalXML(*xml.Encoder, xml.StartElement) error` or `MarshalText` for XML, and `GobEncode() ([]byte, error)` or `MarshalBinary() ([]byte, error)` for gob, a method promoted from an embedded field included, keeps the methods the encoder resolves by name and no field, and the walk does not enter its fields. A method in the method set of a pointer to the type and not of the type itself counts only where every value of the type the walk meets is addressable: reached through a pointer, as a slice element, or as an array element or a field of an addressable value, and not as the value handed to the destination, a map key or value, or a value an interface-typed place holds (as [`reflect.Value.CanAddr`](https://pkg.go.dev/reflect#Value.CanAddr) states). A function or method of a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, and that no destination of this class names one by one, whose name starts with `Unmarshal`, `Decode`, `Bind`, `ShouldBind` or `MustBind`, is, at each of its empty-interface parameters, a destination that reads no field, keeps the encoding and decoding methods of both directions and the methods its package can name, as any outside destination does, and fills every field an encoder would read of each type reached. That holds unless the callee's body, read from the source its package was compiled from, passes that parameter, unchanged or converted to an interface type, to a destination of this class that reads fields or to a function of `fmt`, `log`, `log/slog` or `testing`, which makes it the outside destination that reads every field. A function of the program that forwards an empty-interface parameter to a filling parameter fills at that parameter too. A field such a destination fills and that no class retains in any configuration is reported at the reachability class `possible`, whatever its code. A type assertion `x.(I)`, I an interface type, whose operand is a call of `Interface` on a `reflect.Value` that holds a field of a struct, read by `Field`, `FieldByIndex`, `FieldByName` or `FieldByNameFunc` on a `reflect.Value` holding a value of that struct type (given by `reflect.ValueOf` on an operand of a non-interface type, through `Elem` and `reflect.Indirect`, each through a local of type `reflect.Value` the enclosing body assigns), retains, for each exported field of the struct whose type implements I as `types.Implements` decides, the methods of that type I requires. An unexported field is not read so, because `Interface` panics on it.

exemptions.rule: A type whose values reach a formatting facility that calls its string or error method has that method retained, on the operand's own type and on every type the facility walks to beneath it: the facility invokes `String` or `Error` through an interface at runtime, so the method has no static reference.
exemptions.retains: The `String() string` and `Error() string` methods of the operand's type and of every defined type reached from it through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, an embedded field, exported or not, or an exported struct field, the exported fields of a defined struct type and of a struct type with no name included, at any depth. The reach stops at an interface-typed field.

mechanism.go: A value of type T is an operand of a function that formats its operands with the `fmt` machinery, under a verb valid for a string operand (`%v`, `%s`, `%q`, `%x`, `%X`, the wrapping verb `%w` of `fmt.Errorf`, and the verb-less print forms). Retain T's `String() string` and `Error() string` methods, and retain the same two methods on every defined type reached from T through a pointer, an array, a slice, a map key or value, an embedded field, exported or not, or an exported struct field, applied until no further type joins. The walk enters every type it reaches, so it walks the exported fields of a defined struct type it reaches as it walks the operand's own, and the fields of a struct type with no name as well. The walk is needed because the machinery formats an exported field at any depth and calls the field type's own `String` or `Error` method there. It stops at an interface-typed field, whose dynamic type the analysis does not see, and it does not enter an unexported field that is not embedded, which the machinery prints without calling a method on it. An embedded field is entered whether or not it is exported, because its methods are promoted to the type that embeds it and the machinery calls them through that type. The functions are the `fmt` print, format and error-construction functions (`Print`, `Println`, `Printf`, `Sprint`, `Sprintln`, `Sprintf`, `Fprint`, `Fprintln`, `Fprintf`, `Append`, `Appendln`, `Appendf`, `Errorf`), the `log` package's print, fatal and panic functions and the same methods of `*log.Logger`, the `testing.TB` methods `Log`, `Logf`, `Error`, `Errorf`, `Fatal`, `Fatalf`, `Skip` and `Skipf`, the `log/slog` logging functions and `*slog.Logger` methods (`Debug`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`, their context forms, `Log` and `LogAttrs`), `slog.With`, `(*slog.Logger).With` and `(*slog.Record).Add`, and the `slog.Any`, `slog.Group` and `slog.Attr`-constructing functions, and any function of the analyzed program whose final parameter is variadic `...any` and which passes that parameter, or a format string together with it, to one of the functions in this list, applied until no further function joins. A format string that is not a constant binds every operand of the call. An operand of a `log/slog` logging function reaches this class and `encoding-reflection` both. A method that satisfies `io.Writer` or `http.RoundTripper` is retained by `interface-satisfaction`, not by this class.

exemptions.rule: The standard error helpers reach comparison and unwrapping methods by duck typing rather than through a declared interface, so those methods have no static reference and are retained on any type the program uses as an error.
exemptions.retains: Methods with signature `Is(error) bool`, `As(any) bool`, `Unwrap() error` or `Unwrap() []error` on a type reachable as an error.

mechanism.go: A type is reachable as an error when a value of it enters the conversion set with `error` as the interface. It is reachable as well when a value of it enters the set with an interface I, and the set holds a chain of sites from I to `error`: a site converting a value of type I to `error`, or to an interface that itself begins such a chain, so that each site's value has the interface type the previous site converts to. The type, the first site and the chain are held as `interface-satisfaction` holds a site derived from other sites: by every declaration that holds one of the sites, a use by each of them under reference-counting, and under reachability reachable as an error that way only while each of them is live. Where one of them is dead, a method only such chains retain falls into that declaration's dead component. A site of the chain written in a test file is evidence in a test file. On such a type retain every method whose name and signature match one of the four forms `errors.Is`, `errors.As` and `errors.Unwrap` call.

exemptions.rule: A member of an enumerated type whose values can arrive by conversion rather than by name is never dead in isolation. When the type carries a string, text or binary conversion method, or a value of the type is produced from an integer or from a decoded wire value, every member of that type is retained, so that a member reached only by value is never reported.
exemptions.retains: Every member of the enumerated type.

mechanism.go: The enumerated type is a defined type the target declares whose constants are declared in an `iota` group. A group whose constants carry a type declared in no file under the target root, a standard-library or a module cache type among them, is no enumerated type of the target: the class retains none of its members, and reading that type's methods needs no source outside the target. The class fires when the type has a `String`, `MarshalText`, `UnmarshalText`, `MarshalJSON` or `UnmarshalJSON` method, or when a value of the type is produced by a conversion from an integer type or from a decoded value (an `encoding/json` or `encoding/xml` target, a `database/sql` scan target, a `strconv` result). Retain every constant of the type.
mechanism.ts: The enumerated type is an `enum` declaration. The class fires when a value of the enum is produced by a type assertion from `number` or `string`, by the reverse mapping `E[n]`, or by a decoded value typed as `E`. Retain every member of the enum.

exemptions.rule: Every declaration in a generated file is retained by default, because the generator owns the file and a deletion there is undone at the next generation. When a project configures generated files as included, the analyzer reports findings in them instead and marks each such finding as one no mechanical edit may act on.

mechanism.go: A file is generated when it carries the standard Go generated-code header: a line matching `^// Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT\.$` that appears before the first non-comment, non-blank text of the file, which is the rule `go/ast.IsGenerated` implements. When generated files are configured as included, each finding in one carries `generated: true` and `fixability: none`.
mechanism.ts: A file is generated when its leading comments, the comments before its first token, hold a line of the Go header form, matching `^// Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT\.$`, or the documentation tag `@generated` as a word of a comment, or a notice across the leading comments that holds the word `generated` together with `do not edit`, `will be overwritten` or `should not make any changes`, compared without regard to case, or a first leading comment that starts `// Generated by` and a name, or when it is below a directory that an applied convention row names as generated, as grammar/analysis.md states. A comment after the first token marks nothing. Retain every declaration in the file, recording the file's first line with a detail naming the header, the tag or the row. When generated files are configured as included, each finding in one carries `generated: true` and `fixability: none`.

exemptions.rule: A symbol that another compilation unit reaches by name outside the type checker's view is retained: a symbol an assembly file names, or an exported symbol of a package whose shape is a plugin's. A linker-level alias and a symbol exported to C are roots of the analysis rather than exemptions, so this class retains neither.
exemptions.retains: The symbol an assembly file names, and every exported function and variable of a plugin's main package.

mechanism.go: Retain a symbol named by a `TEXT ·name` directive in an assembly file of the same package, and an exported function or variable of a main package that declares no `main` function, which is the shape of a plugin's main package. A name a `plugin` `Lookup` call carries is retained by `reflective-lookup` in the package that holds the call.

exemptions.rule: Where the project configures template directories, or holds a component file, a member whose name appears in a template or in a component file's markup as a field or method reference is retained at the lowest confidence, and the exemption names the template site that matched. Where the language's template grammar has action delimiters, the project configures the pair the scan reads and the grammar's own pair stands where it does not. The evidence is a text match, not a type relation, so this is a weak class and it applies only where the project asked for it or holds markup no other rule reads.
exemptions.retains: The member of any kind whose name the template references, on any type, an enum member and a static member included.

mechanism.go: Scan every file under the configured template directories, parsed with the action delimiters the configuration sets in `analysis.template_delimiters` and with the `text/template` delimiters `{{` and `}}` where it sets none, and retain every exported field and method whose name appears as a field or method reference in any form the template grammar records: a field reference on the dot, on a variable, or on the result of a parenthesized pipeline or of a call, at every position of a chain, so that `.Page.Title` names `Page` and `Title`. Record the template file and line.
mechanism.ts: Scan every file under the configured template directories, and the markup of every live component file, for the member's name in an interpolation or binding position. Retain every member so named, recording the template file and line.

exemptions.rule: A symbol whose name appears as a string literal that reaches a reflective lookup call is retained at the lowest confidence, and the exemption names the lookup site. A lookup through a receiver whose type maps every string key to one value type reads that mapping rather than a member, so it retains nothing. The evidence is a string match beside a call, not a type relation, so this is a weak class. A method of a defined type T is retained where a string literal spells its name in a call that passes a value of T or a pointer to one to a function or method outside the analyzed program, which a router registering a handler by its method name resolves by reflection.
exemptions.retains: The method, field or member whose name matches the string literal.

mechanism.go: A string literal equal to a method or field name is, or is a constant that flows into, an argument of `MethodByName` or `FieldByName` on a `reflect.Value` or `reflect.Type`, or of a `Lookup` method that resolves a name at runtime. Retain the matching method or field, recording the call site. In a call of a function or method of a package that is neither the target nor a loaded consumer, each argument that is a constant string names methods, and each other argument whose type is a defined non-interface type T of the program, or a pointer to one, is a receiver: the call retains each exported method in the method set of `*T` that the string names. Each item of the string, the items being separated by semicolons, names one identifier, the text after the item's last `:` (the verbs a route maps to the method), with surrounding spaces trimmed. The evidence is a string beside a value, so the class records the call site.
mechanism.ts: A string literal equal to a member name is the index of an element access (`obj["name"]`) whose receiver's type is `any` or declares no string index signature, or an argument of a `Reflect` call (`Reflect.get`, `Reflect.set`, `Reflect.has`) of the global `Reflect`, which a declaration of the target that merges into it, such as a namespace a `declare global` block declares, leaves the global one. A `Reflect` every declaration of which is in the target's files shadows the global one, and a call of it is no reflective lookup. Retain the matching member, recording the site. An element access whose receiver's type declares a string index signature, `Record<string, unknown>` among them, reads the signature and retains nothing.

exemptions.rule: A member that carries a decorator, or whose class carries a decorator, is retained: the decorator receives the member or the class at runtime and may reach the member by name, so the decorator's own symbol counts as a reference to what it decorates.
exemptions.retains: The decorated member, and every member of a decorated class that a decorator can name at runtime.

mechanism.ts: A member is retained when a decorator expression is attached to it, or when a decorator expression is attached to its class. A decorator on a constructor parameter is attached to the parameter and to no member, the parameter property it declares included, because the runtime hands it the constructor and the parameter's position and never a member's name. A decorator on a class retains no member a parameter property of its constructor declares: the code the decorator runs may construct the class, which keeps the parameter, and the member is judged under DS1301. The retention covers `private` members, which a decorator can reach by name, and never `#private` ones.

exemptions.rule: Where the project configures a dependency-injection container, a class the container constructs has its constructor and the members the container injects retained, because the container instantiates the class and populates those members with no reference in the program's own code. A class is constructed by the container when it is registered with it or when a parameter of its constructor carries a decorator. A property or an accessor carrying a decorator does not by itself make its class one the container constructs. The container passes every argument of the constructor it calls, so each parameter property of that constructor is a member it injects, decorated or not.
exemptions.retains: The class's constructor and every injected member: each property and accessor of the class, or of a class it extends, that carries a decorator, and each parameter property of the constructor of the class or of a class it extends.

mechanism.ts: The class is passed to a call of a declaration `ts.injection_registrations` names, or a parameter of its constructor carries a decorator. A decorated property or accessor of a class that neither route reaches makes no class container-constructed. For a class either route reaches, retain the constructor, each property and accessor that carries a decorator, and each parameter property its constructor declares, on the class and on every class it extends.

exemptions.rule: Where the project declares a framework, a member whose name matches that framework's lifecycle contract, on a class reachable as that framework's component, is retained, because the framework calls it by name.

mechanism.ts: The project declares a framework and that framework's lifecycle member names as an entry of `ts.lifecycle_contracts`. A member whose name is in that entry's list is retained when its class is reachable as a component of that framework, by registration, by a decorator or by extending a declaration the entry's `bases` names.

exemptions.rule: A value that flows into a serializer or a schema validator has its data members retained, because the serializer reads them by name at runtime: the data members of every class, interface and object type its static type names, or a `satisfies` expression or a type assertion checks it against, and of every such type reached from those members' types, because the serializer walks the value it is given whatever declared the value's type. Those destinations retain one method, `toJSON`, which a serializer calls on a value that carries one, and no other. A destination outside the analyzed program retains more: a value passed to a parameter typed `unknown` or `any`, a rest parameter whose element type is one of them included, or typed by a type parameter of the function that nothing constrains, or that `unknown` or `any` constrains, of a function the analyzed program does not declare, or declares only ambiently and does not implement, has left the analysis, so its data members are retained together with the two conversion methods a serializer or a formatter resolves by name. A value the program stores in a property, an index signature or an array element of a walked type, or in a variable the argument names, flows into the destination with the value that holds it, so it is walked at its own static type as well, because the serializer emits the value the slot holds: a subtype's members where the slot's type names a supertype, `object`, `unknown` or `any`. A value the program stores in a property typed `unknown` or `any` of an object type the analyzed program does not declare has left the analysis as well, because the code that declares the type receives the object and may serialize what the property holds. A data member is retained only where a write of production code stores into it, a test's write counting too in the run that counts test references, an assignment, a property an object literal writes, a constructor's parameter property, a class property's initializer, or a member an object literal's spread or an `Object.assign` call of the standard library copies from a value whose type has a member of that name, or where a decode of production code fills it: a generic declared outside the analysis that returns it, or a value a `JSON.parse` call returns, or that any other call or a property types as `any` or `unknown`, read as the type through an `as` or angle-bracket assertion around it or by the position it is written in, the annotation of the variable it initializes, the declared result of the function it is returned from, the target of an assignment or the parameter of a call, or that of the call a callback returning it is passed to, a `satisfies` check typing no value, because the receiver reads only what the value carries, so a member nobody writes is reported though its type is serialized. A method and an accessor are retained as stated.
exemptions.retains: The data members of every class, interface and object type the value's static type, or a type a `satisfies` expression or a type assertion checks it against, names and of every such type reached from their members' types, being a class's properties and an interface's or an object type's property signatures. The same members of the static type, and of the checked types, of each value the program stores in a slot of a walked type or in a variable the argument names, and of each value it stores in an `unknown`-typed or `any`-typed property of an object type the analyzed program does not declare. The `toJSON` member of each of those types, a method or a getter, and the `toString` member as well for a destination outside the analyzed program, a callee declared only ambiently and implemented by no code of the analysis included. No other method and no other accessor. A data member only where a write of production code stores into it, a test's write counting too in the run that counts test references, or a decode of production code fills it.

mechanism.ts: A value is an argument of `JSON.stringify` or of a declaration `ts.serializers` names. Take the value's static type and walk it: a union or an intersection walks each constituent, an array or a tuple walks its element types, and a class, an interface or an object type literal, the object type a type alias declares included, retains its data members, being a class's properties and an interface's or an object type literal's property signatures, and its `toJSON` member, a method or a getter, because a serializer reads the name and calls what it answers (ECMA-262 SerializeJSONProperty, step 2), and the same holds for `toString`, then walks each retained data member's type and each index signature's value type, applied until no further type joins. Where the value is written as a `satisfies` expression or a type assertion, an `as` expression or an angle-bracket one, through parentheses and any further such expressions, the walk starts as well from the type each of them names and from the static type of the innermost operand, because the static type of an object literal a `satisfies` expression checks is the literal's own, whose members are not those of the type its properties write, and an assertion to `unknown` or `any` hides the operand's type. An inner assertion's type is taken at its word, as the outermost one's is. The walk stops at a type parameter, whose members the analysis does not see. At a property or a property signature of a walked type, an index signature of a walked type and the element of a walked array type, it walks as well the static type of each value the program stores there and the types that value is checked against as an argument's are, whatever type the slot declares, applied until no further type joins, because a value stored in a slot whose type is a supertype, `object`, `unknown` or `any` is emitted at its own type. A property stores its initializer, the value an object literal whose contextual type is the walked type writes for it, and the right side of each assignment to it through a value of the walked type. An index signature stores the value such an object literal writes for a name the type declares no property under, and the right side of each assignment to an element access, on a value of the walked type, whose index names no declared property. An array element stores each element of an array literal whose contextual type is the walked type, each argument of `push` and `unshift` called on a value of it, and the right side of each assignment to an element access on such a value. An assignment here is a destructuring assignment too: each target of its pattern stores the matching element or property of an array or object literal on the right, else the part of the right side's static type the target's place in the pattern names. A value of the walked type is one whose type the checker reports identical to it, so two containers of one type share what either stores, a modelling bound that retains more and never less. Where the argument itself is a variable that carries a type annotation, or neither an annotation nor an initializer, its stored values are its initializer and the right side of each assignment to it, a destructuring one included, walked in the same way. Those destinations retain no other method and no other accessor. A value passed to a parameter typed `unknown` or `any`, or to a rest parameter whose element type is `unknown` or `any`, such as `console.log(...data: any[])`, of a function or method each of whose declarations that holds the declaration of the call's resolved signature, or each of its declarations where none does, is either outside the files of the project and of the declared consumers, the compiler's library declarations included, or ambient, being in a declaration file or under `declare`, is a destination too, recorded at the call with the detail naming the callee: retain by the same walk the same data members and each walked type's `toJSON` and `toString` members, which a serializer and a formatter resolve by the value's own shape, and no other member. A call through `call`, `apply` or `bind` is a call of the function where some declaration of the method is the compiler's library declaration of `Function`, `CallableFunction` or `NewableFunction`, so a member the target merges into one of those interfaces does not stop it. An ambient declaration has no body the analysis reads, so a member a declaration file of the project merges into a platform interface, such as `postMessage` on a worker's `Client`, leaves its callee outside the analysis. An ambient member of an interface or an object type is not outside where code of the analysis implements that type: a class of those files whose `implements` or `extends` clause names it or a type that extends it, or an object literal of those files that a variable or property annotation, a `satisfies` expression or an `as` expression types as one of them, because that code is what the call runs. A member of a class declared ambiently stays outside whether or not a class of the analysis overrides it, and an object literal typed as the interface any other way, such as by a return or an argument position, implements nothing, a modelling bound that retains more and never less. A parameter typed as an interface or as an object type is not this crossing, because the callee's own declaration names the members it reads. A value stored in a property typed `unknown` or `any` of an object type none of whose declarations is in a file of the project or of a declared consumer, by an object literal whose contextual type is that type or has it as a constituent, or by an assignment to the property through a value of that type, is a destination of the same kind, recorded at the store with the detail naming the property: the same walk retains the same members. Whether the code that declares the type serializes the value is not read, so every such store counts, a modelling bound that retains more and never less. A parameter of a function of the project keeps no member name of the value it is given beyond the properties its type names where it is typed `unknown` or `any`, or as an object type with a string index signature, which holds every other member of the value whatever properties the type names beside it, a rest parameter whose element type is one of them included. Any function of the project that passes such a parameter to such a call, or to any other destination of this class, is itself a destination, applied until no further function joins. Such a parameter that its function enumerates, passing it to `Object.keys`, `Object.entries`, `Object.values` or `Object.getOwnPropertyNames`, as a source of `Object.assign`, or to a `for…in` statement, the `Object` named being the standard library's global, in its own body or in a nested function with no name, a callback or one called where it is written, or one whose name its body writes, reads every property of each value passed to it by name, so it is a destination holding back the value's data members, and a function handing such a parameter on is one too. A value that reaches a destination and whose static type names a type parameter of a function of the project, through its union or intersection constituents and its type arguments, carries as well the type each call of that function passes for the parameter, written as a type argument or read from the arguments where the declared parameter type names it, and such a type that is itself a type parameter of the calling function is followed to that function's calls, until no type parameter joins, because the value the call passes is the one serialized, a modelling bound that retains more and never less.
